text:
Yes. Monzo offers overdrafts on personal accounts in the UK if you're eligible.

**Cost**
- The rate is an EAR (effective annual rate) of 19%, 29% or 39%, depending on your credit score. You can see your own rate in the overdraft section of the app.
- As an example, using an arranged overdraft of £1,200 for 30 days at 39.0% EAR/APR (variable) would cost £32.94.
- Monzo says it doesn't charge hidden or late fees, so the EAR and APR are the same.
- The rate is variable. Monzo can change it, but says it will give you notice.

**How it works**
- When you open an account, Monzo does a soft search of your credit file to decide whether it can lend to you. Lenders can't see this search, so it won't affect your chances of getting credit.
- You choose your limit, up to the amount Monzo can offer you. You can change it at any time in the app or switch it off.
- Interest comes out of your account on the first of every month. You can watch it build up in a feed item at the top of your Home tab.

**Unarranged overdrafts**
- If you go over your arranged limit, you enter an unarranged overdraft. Monzo charges the same for this as for your arranged overdraft.
- If you have no arranged overdraft and your balance goes below zero, Monzo charges 39% EAR (variable).
- The monthly cap on unarranged overdraft charges for your current account is £15.50. That figure comes from a version of Monzo's overdraft information document, so check the current terms in the app.

**Short-term use only**
- If you use your overdraft but add no money to the account for over 60 days, Monzo may decide you aren't using it for short-term borrowing. It might then ask you to make a payment into the account.

Some Monzo pages, such as the business and sole-trader ones, show different rates or fees. The figures above are for personal accounts.
